title: Observability-Driven Development
subtitle: Finish a change by observing it in production
summary: Pip adds a new allocation rule and records its decisions while writing it. Tests establish expectations; production telemetry reveals combinations they missed. The investigation narrows to a component, then becomes a regression test and a verified fix.

concepts.title: Instrument while intent is fresh
concepts.body: Pip records the allocation branch and resulting resource assignment while writing the feature. The author still knows which decisions and outcomes matter. Waiting until an incident can require another deployment and another failure before evidence exists. Pip instruments intent while the context is fresh.

concepts.title: Observe after deployment
concepts.body: Pip’s passing tests are followed by a live build comparison. Equivalent routes and the affected feature cohort reveal production latency and error changes. Fast feedback connects unexpected behavior to decisions still fresh in the author’s mind. Pip observes after deployment instead of treating tests as a complete account of live behavior.

concepts.title: Locate before inspecting code
concepts.body: Pip’s trace narrows the delay to serialization under one input combination. Observability locates where and under which circumstances a running system behaves wrongly. A debugger or profiler can then examine that component’s internals in a local reproduction. Pip combines tools at their appropriate scopes.

concepts.title: Tests and telemetry complement each other
concepts.body: Pip turns the production-only combination into a regression test. Tests encode repeatable expectations; telemetry exposes combinations those tests did not represent. Instrumentation then verifies that the fix helps real requests. Pip keeps both feedback sources because neither answers every question alone.

misconceptions.correction: Tests validate known expectations; production feedback exposes additional interactions and validates real-world outcomes.

misconceptions.claim: A trace viewer must replace a source-code debugger.
misconceptions.correction: Traces locate the operation and context; a debugger may then inspect the implementation in detail.

scenario.title: The tests pass, the feature slows down
scenario.context: A new recommendation feature passes CI but increases latency only for large accounts.

options.label: Compare feature cohorts and account size
options.benefit: Can isolate the production condition missing from tests.
options.cost: Requires feature and account context in telemetry.
options.consequence: The production finding can guide both a targeted fix and a regression test.

options.label: Extend the generic unit suite first
options.benefit: Can improve checks for known implementation behavior.
options.cost: May miss the large-account condition unless production evidence guides it.
options.consequence: Additional tests may pass while the same account-size regression persists.

scenario.debrief: Use the observed cohort to focus investigation and then strengthen the regression tests.

quiz.question: When is a useful time to choose feature-specific instrumentation?
options: After deployment, once a failed request identifies every needed field
At the end of the release cycle, independently of feature implementation
While implementing the decisions and expected outcomes
quiz.explanation: The author can capture intent and relevant context before a failure requires emergency instrumentation.

quiz.question: A trace identifies an expensive parser and its triggering input. What may help next?
options: A focused reproduction with a debugger or profiler
A broader scan of all service metrics before examining the isolated parser
Increasing trace retention without using the known triggering input
quiz.explanation: The system-level search has narrowed enough for code-level tools to become useful.

quiz.question: Why compare deployment cohorts after shipping?
options: To treat any difference between cohorts as proof the release is defective
To check intended and unintended effects under actual production conditions
To replace the need to define expected behavior before release
quiz.explanation: Production comparison completes a feedback path that controlled tests cannot fully supply.
